Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the South African openers Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi. Kraigg Brathwaite has the West Indies players in a tight-knit huddle before spreading out to take the field. Kemar Roach is handed the new ball and will start the proceedings in the third innings. Away we go!
... THIRD INNINGS ...

With around 20 minutes of play left in the day and the hopes of possible play tomorrow, it will be intriguing to see South Africa's approach. Will they come out all guns blazing to quickly add a few runs and set a challenging target for the hosts, or will they opt to bat cautiously in the time remaining in the day? Either way, an exciting end to the day's play is on the horizon as the third innings is set to resume shortly.

For South Africa, it was Keshav Maharaj who put in the hard yards with the ball, steadily chipping away at the West Indies' lineup. Kagiso Rabada was fierce in his execution with the second new ball, delivering a devastating spell that further strengthened the Proteas' chances of securing a positive result in this game if weather permits.

The top three West Indies batters got off to promising starts, successfully navigating the tough phases, only to lose their wickets before they could capitalize on those beginnings. Keacy Carty had a great debut with the bat for his 42 off 81 balls but would have surely loved to make the most of it. Jason Holder and Kavem Hodge provided some stability for the hosts this afternoon, but they struggled against the probing lines delivered by the South African bowlers. As a result, wickets fell in quick succession, and the West Indies, who were in a decent position at the start of Day 4, now find themselves facing an uphill battle being bundled up for 233 runs, handing South Africa a hefty lead of 124 runs.

South Africa have taken firm control over the West Indies, coming out all guns blazing and fully capitalizing on the second new ball to bowl out the hosts for just 233 runs. Windies have fallen 124 runs short of the Proteas' first inning score.

Commentary.Commentary: After a frustrating 6-hour wait, we're finally set to get underway on Day 4. With rain forecast for Day 5, a draw seems the most likely outcome. However, if South Africa can make significant inroads during this 2-hour session, they can still push for a victory. 30 overs are scheduled to be bowled in this session. Temba Bavuma and Co. are in a huddle near the ropes before taking their respective places on the field. Kavem Hodge and Jason Holder are all set to resume their innings with Holder taking the first strike. South Africa are starting with spin in the form of Aiden Markram. A slip and a short leg in place. Let's play...
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

UPDATE - 12.35 am IST (7.05 pm GMT, the previous day) - Right then, we finally have a START TIME. Play will commence at 1 am IST (7.30 pm GMT, the previous day), provided there is no further rain. Let's hope the wait has been worthwhile and we’re in for an exciting passage of play ahead.

UPDATE - 12.25 am IST (6.55 pm GMT, the previous day) - Positive news! Both sets of players and support staff have arrived at the ground, but we’re not quite ready for the start of play yet. Another inspection is scheduled in about 10 minutes. The stumps have been erected and if all goes well at the inspection, we could get some action soon. Stay tuned!

UPDATE - 12.12 am IST (6.42 pm GMT, the previous day) - There has been no official word yet regarding the result of the inspection. We’re anticipating an update soon and remain hopeful for a positive outcome. Stick around.

UPDATE - 11.37 pm IST (6.07 pm GMT) - The visuals are looking great! The covers are completely off the ground, and with the inspection just moments away, this is a highly promising development. Reserve umpire Gregory Brathwaite is out there, making sure everything is in order. On the bright side, the weather has cleared up significantly. We could be in for some positive news very soon. Stay tuned for further updates!

UPDATE - 11.15 pm IST (5.45 pm GMT) - Great news! The drizzle has subsided, and the square, including the strip, has been uncovered. The match officials are on the field, inspecting the outfield, while the ground staff work on drying out some damp patches around the square. However, the match officials are not entirely satisfied with the conditions just yet and have scheduled another inspection at 12 am IST (6.30 pm GMT, the previous day), weather permitting. Stick around for more news.

UPDATE - 10.58 pm IST (5.28 pm GMT) - Uh oh! Not a great sight as reserve umpire Gregory Brathwaite is seen with his umbrella up, indicating a faint drizzle has begun. The ground staff are still out there, working diligently to clear the water from the covers, but with the rain back, their job just got even tougher. Nikhil Uttamchandani informs that the drainage at this venue is excellent. However, there's still a significant amount of water accumulated on the covers, which will take time to clear. The waiting game continues!

UPDATE - 10.46 pm IST (5.16 pm GMT) - Yep, we’re all in the same boat, eagerly waiting for the next update. Unfortunately, we’re still awaiting official word on the situation at the venue. At this point, your guess is as good as ours regarding when play might commence. Let's remain hopeful for some good news soon!

UPDATE - 10.07 pm IST (4.37 pm GMT) - Good news! The rain has finally stopped. Match officials have arrived at the ground, and the ground staff are now using the Super Sopper to remove the excess water from the soaked covers before they can be fully removed. However, it’s still quite gloomy, and without any sunshine to help dry up the outfield, the ground staff have a tough job ahead of them. Finally, there's a ray of hope on what has been a frustrating day so far. Let's keep our fingers crossed for some play!

With the weather dominating much of the spotlight in this first Test, it's worth considering how the match could still reach a conclusion - if the weather permits uninterrupted play for at least a day. While a win for the West Indies seems out of reach, South Africa might still have an outside chance to push for victory and avoid a draw. For that to happen, they’ll need to come out firing when play resumes and quickly bowl out the hosts not just once, but twice. It’s a tall order, but cricket is known for delivering surprises when we least expect them!

UPDATE - 9.23 pm IST (3.53 pm GMT) - The drizzle continues, with live visuals showing a persistently gloomy scene at Queen's Park Oval. The match officials and players remain in their hotels as they wait for the weather to improve. According to Nikhil Uttamchandani on air, while the intensity of the rain has not worsened, it has not stopped, prolonging the delay. As we wait, LUNCH has been taken on Day 4. Fingers crossed for a positive update after Lunch!

While we wait for the weather to clear, let’s shift our focus to basketball at the Paris Olympics 2024. The USA's dominance in the sport remains impressive. Their women's team secured a victory against Australia in the semifinals and is now set to face France in the final, aiming for their eighth consecutive Olympic gold medal. On the men's side, the team is also making headlines, seeking to add another gold to their storied Olympic history. Having emerged victorious against Serbia in the semifinal, they will face France in their quest for a fifth straight Olympic title.

UPDATE - 8.25 pm IST (2.55 pm GMT) - The wait continues as the drizzle persists at Queen's Park Oval. Nikhil Uttamchandani on air notes a silver lining - Unlike Day 1, there haven’t been heavy showers, so puddles haven't formed on the outfield. He estimates that once the rain ceases, it might take the ground staff about an hour to prepare the field for play. However, the crucial first step is for the rain to stop. We will keep you posted.

It's time for more updates from the Paris Olympics 2024! The focus now shifts to football, where the Women's Gold Medal match between the United States and Brazil is about to kick off shortly. The USA are aiming to secure their fifth gold medal, hoping to reclaim the title for the first time since 2012. Meanwhile, Brazil have entered their third final in women's Olympic football history. Interestingly, in their previous two finals, they fell short against the USA. Will history repeat itself, or will Brazil break the streak? Well, we shall soon find out with the kickoff scheduled for 8.30 pm IST (3 pm GMT).

UPDATE - 7.49 pm IST (2.19 pm GMT) - Unfortunately, not much has changed since the previous update, as the rain continues to fall steadily and the covers remain securely in place. It's not the start we were hoping for, but all we can do now is wait for the weather to clear up so the ground staff can spring into action and prepare the field for play. Stay tuned for further updates!

As we await further updates from Port of Spain, let's dive into some exciting developments from the Paris Olympics which is in its penultimate day. Last night, South Africa made history at the Stade de France, securing a silver medal in the Men's 4x100 meters relay, the first for the Rainbow Nation in a relay event at the Olympics. In other news, earlier today, France etched its name in the history books with a dominant 3-0 victory over Poland. By doing so, they became the first Men's volleyball team to win back-to-back Olympic golds since the United States achieved this feat in 1984 and 1988.

Folks, you must be wondering what to do now with the rain pattering down at the Queen's Park Oval. Well, fret not, there's plenty of action across the globe to keep you entertained. The Hundred is heating up, with each game in both the Men's and Women's divisions carrying significant weight hereon as teams jostle for a top-three finish. Trent Rockets are currently locking horns with Southern Brave in the Men's fixture, while Birmingham Phoenix are about to take on Welsh Fire in the Women's game. So, while we wait for the weather to clear in Port of Spain, why not switch tabs and dive into these contests?

UPDATE - 6.47 pm IST (1.17 pm GMT) - A dampener on the morning's excitement! It's currently drizzling at Queen's Park Oval, and as a result, the START OF PLAY on Day 4 has been DELAYED. Ian Bishop, on air, informs us that it has been raining since last night in Port of Spain and has continued into this morning. He also mentions that both teams won't be leaving their hotels until 8.45 pm IST (3.15 pm GMT), which means we're in for a delayed start, with play unlikely to commence for at least a couple of hours. Stay tuned for more updates as we wait for clearer skies!

As we enter Day 4, the West Indies trail by 212 runs with six wickets in hand. The onus will be on Hodge and Holder to continue their partnership and close the gap to South Africa's total. For the Proteas, they'll be looking to break this stand quickly and push for a substantial lead, especially with rain looming as a potential factor in the coming days. Stay tuned for what promises to be an engaging day of Test cricket!

As for the West Indies, their bowlers did what was asked of them, cleaning the tail up swiftly. Mikyle Louis, Kraigg Brathwaite, and Keacy Carty all got starts but couldn’t convert them into substantial scores. As the hosts slipped from 114/1 to 124/4, it seemed like another familiar Windies collapse was on the cards. However, Kavem Hodge and Jason Holder held the fort to end the day on a steadier note.

South Africa didn’t begin Day 3 as they had hoped, managing to add only 13 runs to their overnight total, finishing at 357. Keshav Maharaj put in a marathon effort on a placid surface, bowling 28 overs from one end and undoubtedly emerging as the pick of the bowlers with 3 crucial wickets. However, the second session was marred by frequent rain delays, which disrupted the rhythm of the game. Additionally, a few missed opportunities in the field didn’t help South Africa's cause.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of Day 4 of the first Test between the West Indies and South Africa at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain, Trinidad. As we head into Day 4, South Africa hold the upper hand in this rain-affected contest. An intriguing day of Test cricket awaits us, and let’s hope the rain stays away.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that wraps up the proceedings on this 'moving day'. South Africa will reflect on missed opportunities in the field, which could have strengthened their position further. With rain forecast for Days 4 and 5, the visitors will need to be sharp with the ball and in the field to secure a favourable result. West Indies, trailing by 212 runs, will look to the pair currently batting and Joshua Da Silva to narrow the deficit. With the pitch still good for batting, there’s potential for them to close the gap and get closer to parity. It will be yet another early start with the first ball on Day 4 to be bowled at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). As always, you can join us earlier for the build-up. See you then. Cheers!

Keshav Maharaj, the man of the moment for South Africa is in for a chat. He starts by saying that target bowling is really important. Informs that he is glad to be back in the middle and that he loves red ball cricket a lot. Adds that he loves repetition and that works for him. When a new batter comes to the crease, he tries to use different trajectories and pace. Thinks that there is not much support off the surface. In Test cricket, it is needed to bowl consistently in the channel and the rest will take care of itself.

Earlier, South Africa began the day at 344/8 but managed to add just 13 runs to their overnight total, finishing at 357. Wiaan Mulder was left stranded as the tailenders couldn't provide much support. In reply, the West Indies made a cautious yet solid start. Mikyle Louis was the aggressor, capitalizing on loose deliveries, but just as they seemed set to reach Lunch without losing a wicket, Keshav Maharaj struck. He went through the defences of Louis on the final ball before the Lunch break, leaving the West Indies at 53/1 and trailing by 304 runs.

The second session was disrupted by three lengthy rain delays, allowing for only 22.2 overs of play. Keacy Carty, making his Test debut, appeared busy and confident at number 3. Kraigg Brathwaite, who was dropped on 7 by Aiden Markram, found his rhythm after the early scare. However, with rain looming, a moment of casual running saw Brathwaite run out, providing South Africa with a much-needed opening. Unfortunately for them, the chance to capitalize on that wicket was cut short as a heavy downpour forced an early end to the session.

End of another attritional day of Test cricket, marked by weather interruptions that allowed only 71.4 overs of play. The day began with the match hanging in the balance, but a disciplined South African bowling attack, spearheaded by Keshav Maharaj, who bowled 28 overs unchanged from one end, has tipped the scales in favour of the visitors. As the third session got underway, Maharaj continued his fine form. He first dismissed the set batter Keacy Carty and then nicked Alick Athanaze off, a well-deserved reward for his relentless efforts throughout the day. The West Indies, once comfortable at 114/1, suddenly found themselves at 124/4. Kavem Hodge and Jason Holder then steadied the ship, ensuring no further setbacks. Hodge, however, had a stroke of luck, having been dropped on 3 by Kyle Verreynne off Aiden Markram's bowling.

Talking about the post-Lunch session, we were all set to begin the proceedings post-Lunch, but as soon as the umpires set their foot on the field, the rain started to pour down, forcing the players to head back into the pavilion. There was almost a 55-minute delay, which was followed by just one single over from Kagiso Rabada post which the umpires once again took the call of bringing the game to a halt as a precaution. Finally, then we were blessed with some cricket, for almost an hour and 15 minutes, before the smiles were wiped off our faces once again. Kraigg Brathwaite and Keacy Carty came out with the right intent in this session and started to attack the spinner from the get-go here. South Africa stuck to their main apin arsenal in Keshav Maharaj who kept attacking from one end through the innings. He was certainly troubling the two batters, with his variations. He also created a couple of chances but the Proteas failed to convert them in their favour. The momentum though is undoubtedly with the visitors here, as they got rid of a resilient batter in Kraigg Brathwaite. Is this the opening that South Africa were waiting for? Will they even get a chance to capitalize on it? We don't know yet, as it is pelting down here. So, do stay tuned for further updates.

OH NO! West Indies lost their first wicket at the brink of the Lunch Break, and they have lost their second wicket, at the brink of Tea. Kraigg Brathwaite this is the man who has to head back to the dressing room here. It was all looking good from the West Indies' point of view, with the way they negotiated this tricky phase, post lunch, which saw plenty of rain already. But once again, they have dug a hole for themselves here. We would've seen a new batter come in, but well, the rains are back in fine fashion here, to spoil our mood once again. The players are running off, as the rain intensifies. Groundstaff, once again, has been on the money here, as they cover the main pitch, and square areas in a jiffy.

OUT RUN OUT! Excellent effort by Wiaan Mulder! Lackadaisical running by the Windies skipper and he pays the ultimate price. Lungi Ngidi bowls it full and honing in at the stumps, Kraigg Brathwaite gets his weight on the front foot and clips it to the right of mid on. He times it well, resulting in the ball travelling to the fielder quickly and he sets off for a risky single. Wiaan Mulder swoops in, picks it up and hits the stumps at the bowling end. South Africa do not look too interested as the decision is referred upstairs. The replays show that Brathwaite had no part of his bat inside the crease when the bails were dislodged. Moreover, the Windies skipper did not stretch forward fully and plonked his bat instead of sliding it in. Also, the replays show that he ran sideways rather than running in a straight line, resulting in him falling just short of his crease at the bowling end. It turns out that Ngidi had overstepped but it does not affect the run out dismissal in any way. South Africa are delighted as they have finally managed to break this stand. Brathwaite goes for 35. The 61-run stand is broken and West Indies are 114/2. Just as OUT flashed on the big screen, heavens opened up, forcing the umpires to take the players off. It will be TEA on DAY 3!

Temba Bavuma then handed the ball to Keshav Maharaj and he managed to find some turn right away. The pacers troubled the batters with disciplined bowling while Maharaj worked his magic at the other end. He finally managed to get a breakthrough and gave them a bit of relief right before lunch. The Proteas would be much more confident returning back to the field after Lunch while the Windies will have to discuss some strategies. Play will resume with the start of Session Two in a short time. The players will walk back out at 10.10 pm IST (4.40 pm GMT).

The session started with Jomel Warrican and Jayden Seales cleaning things up for South Africa for a score of 357. The next innings started off slowly with the bowlers creating pressure on Kraigg Brathwaite and Mikyle Louis, the openers for West Indies. They created a few chances but they failed to get an early wicket here. Mikyle Louis was looking in good touch with his timing with Brathwaite supporting him at the other end.

Keshav Maharaj does the trick and draws first blood with the wicket of Mikyle Louis just before Lunch. Louis will be disappointed with himself because he was looking strong out in the middle. The scoreboard for West Indies reads 53/1 in 27 overs trailing by 304 runs.

OUT! TIMBER! Right at the brink of Lunch, Keshav steps up for his side and finds the breakthrough. This is an arm ball, that lands around off, and keeps going on straight. Mikyle Louis gets on his front foot and tries to defend it out but ends up playing the wrong line completely. The ball sneaks past the inside edge and goes on to crash into the stumps. Keshav Maharaj is pumped up, and the boys join him to begin the celebration. Mikyle Louis looks at the heavens and trudges back to the dressing room.
